lead: Counting is under way after Wednesday's local government elections, with very early results showing the ANC and DA neck and neck nationally and Durban still to report; final results are expected on Sunday. Abroad, Democrats have taken both houses of the US Congress.

items.title: Early local election count shows ANC and DA running close
items.summary: With only around 4% of voting districts counted by 2:35am, the ANC had about 34.8% of the PR vote and the DA 32.4%, with turnout near 48%. These figures are provisional and will shift sharply as counting continues.

items.title: What's at stake: 29.2 million voters, 257 councils, results due Sunday
items.summary: Voters chose 8 metro, 44 district and 205 local councils, which will then elect mayors. The vote is seen as a test for the ANC, and it is MK's first municipal election; final results are expected on Sunday.

items.title: eThekwini: about 2 million voters in a key MK-versus-ANC contest
items.summary: Sixty-nine parties and 14 independents contested Durban, where the ANC has relied on smaller partners since losing its majority in 2021. MK fielded Mxolisi Phakathi for mayor; the DA's candidate is Hanif Hoosen and ActionSA's is Zwakele Mncwango.

items.title: Small parties could decide who governs Durban's 224-seat council
items.summary: A majority needs 113 seats, and analysts expect around ten small parties to determine whether an MK-led or DA-led bloc takes control. Water supply was the dominant campaign issue in the metro.

items.title: Ballots and security stamp stolen from Botha's Hill voting station
items.summary: Unmarked ballots and a ward stamp were taken from Mnyameni Secondary School the night before the vote. The IEC issued a new stamp with a different code so any stolen ballots can be identified at counting, and police are investigating.

items.title: Rain-damaged roads kept two Umzumbe voting stations closed
items.summary: Heavy rain washed away access roads to stations in Umzumbe on the KZN South Coast, and police and the SANDF worked to reach them. One of three affected stations had been reached by the time of the IEC briefing.

items.title: Severe thunderstorm warning for most of KZN today
items.summary: The Weather Service has a yellow level 4 warning for severe storms across KZN except the far northeast, with risks of flooding, hail and power outages. Eastern areas are also expected to be hot and very humid.

items.title: ANC leadership to decide coalition deals centrally
items.summary: The ANC has signalled that its national leadership, not regional structures, will pick coalition partners after the results. Coalition decisions are due within about three weeks across several metros and many councils.

items.title: Democrats win control of both the US Senate and House
items.summary: Democrats flipped Senate seats including Texas, Maine, Ohio and North Carolina, securing at least 54 seats, and are projected to take the House. Alaska and Mississippi were still undecided on Wednesday.

items.title: Vance blames the Iran war for Republican midterm losses
items.summary: Vice President JD Vance publicly questioned whether the war with Iran was worth it and linked it to the defeat. Trump accepted the war was a factor but said he would make the same decision again.

items.title: Iran claims four tankers hit mines near Hormuz; Trump says no immediate strikes
items.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said four tankers struck mines south of the Strait of Hormuz, a claim not independently verified. Trump later said there were no immediate plans to strike Iran, and Brent slid to about $93.

items.title: Israel certifies election result, rejecting Likud fraud claims
items.summary: The election committee found no irregularities that changed the outcome. Netanyahu's bloc has 53 seats and Gadi Eisenkot's 48, both short of 61, so President Herzog will now consult parties on who should try to form a government.

items.title: DR Congo Ebola outbreak passes 10,000 confirmed cases
items.summary: By 28 October the outbreak had 10,305 confirmed cases and 4,996 deaths, making it the second-largest on record. The US now requires air passengers to confirm they have not been in the DRC in the past 21 days.

items.title: Rand firms about 1% as US midterm result weighs on the dollar
items.summary: The rand traded near R16.42 to the dollar on Wednesday, about 1.1% stronger on the day. Gold rose more than 3%, and US stocks opened higher after the Democratic sweep.

items.title: What losing AGOA means for South African exporters
items.summary: The US plans to drop SA from AGOA from 2027. Citrus, macadamias and sorbet exporters are most exposed, but minerals are unaffected, and only about 10% of US-bound exports used AGOA in 2025. Minister Parks Tau says SA has 60 days to appeal.

items.title: Oil drops as Democrats sweep Congress
items.summary: Brent fell about 3% to roughly $100 a barrel on Wednesday morning, while the Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq all opened higher.

items.title: David Jones, once owned by Woolworths, enters administration
items.summary: The 188-year-old Australian department store chain went into voluntary administration, and a sale process will start. Woolworths sold it in 2022 to Anchorage Capital, so the SA retailer is no longer involved.

items.title: Boks open November tour against Italy in Genoa on Saturday
items.summary: Rassie Erasmus has a 37-man squad with six uncapped players for Nations Championship Tests against Italy, France on 13 November and Ireland on 21 November, before finals weekend in London. Kolbe, Etzebeth and Pollard are among the injured.

items.title: Sundowns edge Golden Arrows to reach Carling Knockout semis
items.summary: Rayners scored in the 68th minute to give Sundowns a 1-0 quarter-final win over Arrows at Loftus Versfeld.

items.title: Fenerbahce beat Liverpool; Real Madrid win in Athens
items.summary: Fenerbahce beat Liverpool 3-2 in Istanbul in the Champions League, and Real Madrid won 3-2 away at AEK Athens.

items.title: Apple flags risks from autonomous AI agents as Siri opens to developers
items.summary: Apple's annual filing warns that AI agents could exceed their permissions or carry out unauthorised transactions. The warning came as it opened Siri AI to app developers in iOS 27.3 betas.

items.title: Google ties Search to AI tools for school accounts
items.summary: Under new education settings, schools that switch off Google's AI tools also lose Google Search for student accounts. Google says AI is now part of Search.
